reads.source: Gallica f648 whole page plus a wide native crop across both column feet and a 3x blow-up of the single word *funiculu*. Archive.org p.653 rendered at 300 dpi.
reads.found: THE RICHEST PAGE IN THE STINT, and every finding is OURS, not Migne's. (1) 1295D: our twin prints *ante scandalum cruceis, crucis, praemisit* -- which reads as a Pattern 11a dittography with variation. IT IS NOT. The plate hyphenates *cru-* / *cis* across a line break and reads *crucis*, once, on BOTH printings. Our digitization manufactured the doubling. (2) 1295D-1296A: our twin prints the non-word *exallabitur*; the plate hyphenates *exal-* / *tabitur* across the COLUMN break and reads *exaltabitur*, on both printings. A textbook [sic:] withdrawn. (3) 1296D-1297A: our twin ends an *usque ad* tail *qui funiculu.*; archive p.653 prints *qui funiculus.* clean, and the Gallica copy's final s is worn to a dot at 3x. No [sic:]. (4) 1297A: the plate prints VERS. 16. -- with the dash our twin drops. Vulgate divergences fired at 1295D (Is 52:13 verb order), 1296B (Jo 1:29 peccatum sing.), 1296C three times (Lc 8:5 seminat; 1 Pet 2:24 pertulit...super lignum; 1 Cor 9:22 facerem salvos). Foot of both columns blank.

reads.found: ONE [sic:] CANDIDATE WITHDRAWN AT THE SECOND PRINTING. At 1297B our twin and the Gallica copy both read *Ne justus tribu-atus deficiat* -- the non-word *tribuatus*, hyphenated at the line break, with *tribulatus* obviously wanted. Archive p.654 prints *tribu-latus* CLEAN over the same break. Two printings, one sound: no marker fired, and the English renders 'lest the just man, being afflicted, fail'. Otherwise no plate/TEI divergence in either column. Vulgate divergences fired at 1297D (Eccle 11:1 transeuntes aquas / post tempora multa) and 1298C (Rom 12:1 hostiam viventem, sanctam, Deo placentem); three more logged as immaterial and declined (Jo 15:19 essetis for fuissetis and idcirco for propterea; Rom 10:12 Sed non est for Non enim est). Pattern 8 confirmed at the foot of col 1297: the sentence ending *praemia recipies* carries NO terminal stop on the plate, exactly as our twin has it. Foot of both columns blank.
